| Type of Error | Causes |

questions.questionText: According to the ACR BI-RADS Atlas® 5th Edition, which description of the Kinetic Curve Assessment is **not** true?

options.text: In initial phase, slow is deﬁned as an increase in signal intensity of less than 50% within the ﬁrst 2 minutes

During the delayed phase, washout is deﬁned as a decrease of more than 10% from the highest signal intensity during the initial rise. Washout curves are speciﬁcally denoted “suspicious.”

questions.reference: ACR BI-RADS Atlas® 5th Edition；10.2214/AJR.15.15957；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p2

【2021 官方詳解】

It represents the initial increase in contrast enhancement in the kinetic assessment for BI-RADS. An intensity increase < 50% is classified as slow, 50–100% as medium, and > 100% as fast enhancement. SER indicates the kinetic curve shape that represents the delayed phase in BI-RADS assessment. Persistent is more than 10% of initial enhancement, washout is less than 10% of initial enhancement, and plateau is between the two.
10.2214/AJR.15.15957
The kinetic curve can be classified into three categories. Early enhancement (2 minutes after agent injection), during which the initial rise of the enhanced curve can be divided into “slow”, “medium”, and “rapid”.
The signal intensity 2 minutes after contrast injection is defined as “delayed phase, which is divided into “persistent” (type I), “plateau” (type II), and “washout” (type III)

= excess iron deposition in tissues (hemosiderosis) resulting in tissue injury

= autosomal recessive genetic disorder (abnormal iron-loading gene on short arm of chromosome 6) in thalassemia, sideroblastic anemia

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is **false** about anomalous origin of coronary artery?

options.text: The ALCAPA syndrome (anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery) is among the differential diagnoses for massive cardiomegaly in the newborn
Artery courses downward (hammock sign) below the crista supraventricularis in interarterial course
Prepulmonic coronary arteries are particularly common in tetralogy of Fallot (D)Transseptal course does not have an oblong or slitlike orifice

questions.reference: Identifying, Characterizing, and Classifying Congenital Anomalies of the Coronary Arteries; RadioGraphics 2012; 32:453–468；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p18
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Artery courses downward (hammock sign) below the crista supraventricularis in Transseptal Variant.
Origin from the Pulmonary Artery
Origin of a coronary artery from the pulmonary artery is usually discovered owing to severe clinical manifestations. In this entity, the LMCA more commonly originates from the pulmonary artery. This pattern was described in 1956 and retains the eponym of the authors who described it (Bland-Garland-White syndrome). This entity is also known by the acronym ALCAPA (anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery). Since its initial description, ALCAPA has been recognized to constitute 0.25%–0.5% of cases of congenital heart disease
Patients usually present with symptoms of myocardial ischemia or with left ventricular volume overload due to left-to-right shunting. The entire coronary arterial system is usually markedly enlarged and tortuous as a result of increased flow. ALCAPA syndrome is among the differential diagnoses for massive cardiomegaly in the newborn period, a finding that is one of the classic features of this entity at presentation
Prepulmonic Course
Normally, the major coronary arteries are never found in a position anterior to the pulmonary outflow tract or pulmonary artery. When a prepulmonic artery is present, it usually poses no hemodynamic consequences, although some case reports posit an association with angina (52).
Prepulmonic coronary arteries are particularly common in tetralogy of Fallot, in which the prepulmonic artery may complicate the surgical approach to correction of pulmonary outflow tract stenosis (53). Usually, the prepulmonic vessel is the LMCA (Fig 11), although the RCA may originate from the LAD artery or LMCA and subsequently take a prepulmonic course
Interarterial Course
Several reasons have been suggested for the association between interarterial coronary arteries and sudden cardiac death. It has been postulated that interarterial coronary arteries tend to have a more slitlike orifice and that the slitlike orifice is more prone to occlusion.

**Table 1. Moyamoya syndrome-associated diseases and conditions**

| 分組 | 疾病 |
|---|---|

**Table 1. CT Radiation Dose Parameters**

| Dose Parameter | Definition | Effects on Radiation Dose | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tube potential or voltage | X-ray beam energy | Proportional to square of tube voltage change | kV |
| Product of tube current and time | Photon fluence; number of photons in defined exposure time | Directly proportional to radiation dose | mAs |
| Pitch | Ratio of table feed per gantry rotation to nominal width of beam collimation | Inversely proportional to radiation dose | - |
| CTDIw | Average radiation dose in scan volume measured in standard CT phantoms; 1/3 CTDI center + 2/3 CTDI periphery | Directly proportional to radiation dose in unit volume, influenced by pitch factor | mGy |
| CTDIvol | CTDIw/pitch | Directly proportional to radiation dose in unit volume, irrespective of pitch factor | mGy |
| Dose-length product | CTDIvol x scan length (cm) | Directly proportional to total scanned radiation dose | mGy·cm |
| Effective dose | Overall risk-related radiation exposure; Σ W_T (tissue weighting factor) x H_T (tissue equivalent dose) | Directly proportional to total scanned radiation dose and overall risk of irradiated tissue | mSv |

Note — CTDIvol = volume CT dose index, CTDIw = weighted CT dose index

- astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, WHO grade 2
  - a diffusely infiltrative astrocytic glioma with an IDH1 or IDH2 mutation that is well-differentiated and lacks histologic features of anaplasia. Mitotic activity is not detected or low. Microvascular proliferation, necrosis and CDKN2A/B homozygous deletions are absent

  - a diffusely infiltrative astrocytic glioma with an IDH1 or IDH2 mutation that exhibits focal or dispersed anaplasia and displays significant mitotic activity. Microvascular proliferation, necrosis and CDKN2A/B homozygous deletions are absent
- astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, WHO grade 4
  - a diffusely infiltrative astrocytic glioma with an IDH1 or IDH2 mutation that exhibits microvascular proliferation or necrosis or CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion or any combination of these features

imageOcr.markdown:
**Table 1: US Artifacts due to Beam and Resolution Characteristics**

| Type of Artifact | Physics Mechanism | Alteration of Artifacts | Clinical Relevance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Beam width | Poor lateral resolution | Can be reduced by dynamic receive focusing, multiple-transmit FZs, increasing frequency, FZ placement, local speed of sound selection | Lateral blurring of point targets, aberrant echoes from adjacent highly echogenic objects |
| Section thickness | Poor elevational resolution | Can be reduced by positioning the area of interest in FZ with a standoff pad or by using 1.5D/2D transducer arrays | Mimics debris in anechoic structures, aberrant internal echoes in small cysts and vessels |
| Axial resolution | Axial resolution | Better with increasing frequency | Choose a higher frequency for better axial resolution |
| Speckle noise | Acoustic interference causing granular appearance | Can be reduced by SRI, SCI, THI | Degrades spatial and contrast resolution but also gives tissues their characteristic image texture |
| Secondary lobe (Side lobes, Grating lobes) | Echoes transmitted outside primary beam are reflected back to transducer | Can be reduced by THI, decreasing gain, changing AOI, using multiple windows, advanced transducer design | Mimics debris in anechoic structures |

Note — AOI = angle of insonation, FZ = focal zone, 1.5D = 1.5-dimensional, SCI = spatial compound imaging, SRI = speckle reduction imaging, THI = tissue harmonic imaging, 2D = two-dimensional.

imageOcr.markdown:
**Table 3: US Artifacts due to Attenuation Characteristics**

| Type of Artifact | Physics Mechanism | Alteration of Artifacts | Clinical Relevance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Increased through transmission | Increased intensity of echoes distal to a low-attenuating structure | May be increased by using THI | Differentiation of cystic from solid structures |
| Acoustic shadowing (Clean / Partial / Dirty) | Reduction in echo strength distal to a highly attenuating or reflective object | Increases with increased frequency and THI; decreases with inappropriate FZ placement, excessive beam width, and SCI | Detection of stones, calcification, and air |

Note.—FZ = focal zone, SCI = spatial compound imaging.

**Table 2: US Artifacts due to Location (Path or Speed) Characteristics**

| Type of Artifact | Physics Mechanism | Alteration of Artifacts | Clinical Relevance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reverberation | Reflections between highly reflective interfaces in parallel | Can be reduced by using THI, decreasing gain, changing AOI, and using multiple windows | Usually unwanted, mimicking debris within cystic structures; may be useful, as in abnormal air |
| Comet tail | Reverberations from closely spaced highly reflective interfaces | May be more visible using THI and less visible by using SCI | Adenomyomatosis, colloid nodules, calcifications, foreign bodies, surgical clips, IUDs |
| Ring down | Resonant vibrations within air bubbles | May be reduced by using SCI | Abnormal air (abscesses, pneumoperitoneum, PVG, emphysematous infections, pneumobilia, normal air [bowel loops, appendix], B-lines) |
| Mirror image | Reflections off a strong specular reflector produce a mirror image of an object | May be reduced by decreasing gain, changing AOI, using multiple imaging windows | Mimics disease, such as pseudothickened bowel wall and consolidated lung |
| Multipath | Small off-axis reflections on path to or from primary reflector | May be altered by varying AOI or imaging window | General image degradation |
| Refraction (Misregistration, Ghosting, Edge shadowing) | Refraction at oblique interfaces causes altered location of objects, duplication of underlying structures, and/or shadowing at edges | May be reduced by varying AOI or imaging window | False position of lesions during biopsy, can mimic duplication of structures (gestational sac, spinal cord, aorta), cyst characterization by using edge shadowing |
| Speed of sound (Boundary distortion, Misregistration of targets, Errors in size, Phase aberration) | A constant speed of sound is used to calculate depth in soft tissues, but there actually is variability among different tissues | Modern US units allow manual speed of sound correction | Inaccurate locations and measurements of structures in axial dimension, loss of lateral resolution, bayonet artifact |
| Range ambiguity | Echoes deep to imaging range are depicted within range on the next pulse | May be reduced by reducing PRF, reducing the number of FZs, increasing the image depth | Mimics debris in large fluid-filled structures |

Note — AOI = angle of insonation, FZ = focal zone, IUD = intrauterine device, PRF = pulse repetition frequency, PVG = portal venous gas, SCI = spatial compound imaging.

imageOcr.markdown:
**TEACHING POINTS**

- The risk of NSF after GBCA exposure depends on which agent is used, with most cases reported after use of nonionic linear agents.
- Administration of higher than standard doses (>0.1 mmol/kg) of GBCAs has been associated with development of NSF.
- The dramatic reduction of new cases of NSF over the last decade may have occurred because of more routine screening for kidney disease, less use of the GBCAs that have been associated with the most cases of NSF (particularly in patients with renal dysfunction), and less use of the high-dose GBCA-enhanced examinations that were sometimes used in MR angiography.
- To our knowledge, there have been no studies in animals or humans demonstrating clinical, behavioral, or biologic changes associated with neuronal gadolinium deposition.
- Neuronal GBCA deposition has been reported after administration of linear and macrocyclic agents. However, less retention is seen after use of macrocyclic agents.

| | Coherent Scatter | Photoelectric | Compton Scatter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Products | X-Ray photon (=energy) | Electron; Characteristic X-Ray (low energy) | Electron; Scattered Photon (low energy) |
| Outcome | Direction change of x-ray | X-Ray stops and deposits energy locally | Some energy deposited, scattered x-ray in different direction |

Gadoxetate disodium (also known by the tradenames PrimovistTM and EovistTM) is a hepatospecific paramagnetic gadolinium-based contrast agent, used exclusively in MRI liver imaging
- linear, ionic molecule

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about imaging findings of mass-forming pancreatitis and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is WRONG?

options.text: Simultaneous dilatation of the common bile duct and pancreatic duct, known as the double duct sign, favors the diagnosis of a malignancy
Pancreatic parenchymal calcifications are commonly seen in chronic pancreatitis, and peripheral displacement of calcifications can indicate a new underlying malignancy
Soft-tissue attenuation that encases the adjacent vasculature is highly suggestive of the extraglandular spread of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
Smooth narrowing of the pancreatic duct that traverses a pancreatic mass without abrupt obstruction strongly favors the diagnosis of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma

questions.reference: Wolske, K. M., Ponnatapura, J., Kolokythas, O., Burke, L. M. B., Tappouni, R., & Lalwani, N. (2019). Chronic Pancreatitis or Pancreatic Tumor? A Problem-solving Approach. RadioGraphics, 39(7), 1965–1982. https://doi.org/10.1148/rg.2019190011；10.1148/rg.2019190011；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p24
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Smooth narrowing of the pancreatic duct that traverses a pancreatic mass without abrupt obstruction strongly favors the diagnosis of inflammatory mass.

⚠️ 本題含影像（官方詳解 PDF 第 24 頁），影像尚未匯入，判讀請對照原檔。

imageOcr.markdown:
**TEACHING POINTS**

- Smooth narrowing of the pancreatic duct that traverses a pancreatic mass without abrupt obstruction strongly favors the diagnosis of an inflammatory mass.
- Pancreatic parenchymal calcifications are commonly seen in chronic pancreatitis, and peripheral displacement of calcifications can indicate a new underlying malignancy that may otherwise be imaging occult or poorly visualized because of gland heterogeneity from chronic pancreatitis.
- In the absence of the pathognomonic capsulelike rim, visualization of multiple pancreatic or biliary strictures rather than a solitary stricture and absence of substantial dilatation of the side branches or upstream pancreatic duct may be helpful clues that a focal mass in the pancreas represents focal AIP. Similar to other benign focal inflammatory lesions in the pancreas, AIP often shows the duct-penetrating sign, which further supports a benign diagnosis. Extrapancreatic autoimmune disease may be present.
- Displacement rather than encasement of the common bile duct and/or the gastroduodenal artery is highly suggestive of the diagnosis of PDP rather than PDAC.
- Dilatation of both the common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct, or the double duct sign, is highly suggestive of an underlying neoplasm. Although uncommon, inflammatory disease can produce this finding, which mimics malignancy.

questions.questionText: Which of the followings about renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is wrong?

options.text: Clear cell RCC is associated with Von-Hippel-Lindau syndrome
Chromophobe RCC is associated with Birt Hogg Dube syndrome
Papillary RCC is more often associated with lymphangitic spread and peritoneal carcinomatosis
Medullary RCC is an uncommon low-grade neoplasm with imaging appearance of a multilobulated enhanced mass

questions.reference: Radiopedia；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p26
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Hereditary renal cancer syndromes
- von Hippel Lindau syndrome: predominantly clear cell type
- tuberous sclerosis: predominantly clear cell type (also associated with angiomyolipoma)
- Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome: predominantly chromophobe type, oncocytoma, or a hybrid of both
- sickle cell trait or hemoglobin SC disease: renal medullary carcinoma
- hereditary renal oncocytoma: oncocytoma
Pathology
- clear cell renal carcinoma (conventional): 70-80%
- papillary renal cell carcinoma: 13-20%
  - can be multifocal and bilateral
  - most common form in dialysis-associated RCC
- chromophobe renal cell carcinoma: 5%
  - similar histologically to renal oncocytomas 4
  - best prognosis 5
- collecting duct renal cell carcinoma (Bellini duct): <1%
  - worst prognosis 5
- renal medullary carcinoma: rare, highly aggressive.
MRI
- T2: appearances depend on histology 6
  - clear cell RCC: T2 hyperintense
  - papillary RCC: T2 hypointense
- T1 C+ (Gd): often shows prompt arterial enhancement
Clear cell RCC: Pancreatic and renal metastases
Papillary RCC: Lymphangitic spread and peritoneal carcinomatosis
Sarcomatoid transformation in ccRCC: Increased the risk of lymphangitic spread, pleural and peritoneal metastases

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is WRONG?

options.text: Above the hyoid bone, the posterior aspect of the middle layer of the buccopharyngeal fascia continues to the skull base and covers the pharyngeal constrictor muscles. However, above the carotid bifurcation, the contribution of the middle layer to the carotid sheath is inconsistent
The retropharyngeal space extends from the skull base to the thoracocervical junction as the alar fascia attaches to the buccopharyngeal fascia somewhere between the C6 and T4 vertebral levels
If the masticator space is involved, the infection has the potential to extend intracranially through the foramen ovale, along the course of the mandibular nerve

questions.reference: Kamalian, S., Avery, L., Lev, M. H., Schaefer, P. W., Curtin, H. D., & Kamalian, S. (2019). Nontraumatic Head and Neck Emergencies. RadioGraphics, 39(6), 1808–1823. https://doi.org/10.1148/rg.2019190159；10.1148/rg.2019190159；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p33

⚠️ 本題含影像（官方詳解 PDF 第 33 頁），影像尚未匯入，判讀請對照原檔。

imageOcr.markdown:
**TEACHING POINTS**

- Above the hyoid bone, the posterior aspect of the middle layer of the deep cervical fascia (or buccopharyngeal fascia) continues to the skull base and covers the pharyngeal constrictor muscles. However, above the carotid bifurcation, the contribution of the middle layer to the carotid sheath is inconsistent; it does not form a well-defined sheath around the internal and external carotid arteries and the internal jugular vein.
- The retropharyngeal space extends from the skull base to the thoracocervical junction as the alar fascia attaches to the buccopharyngeal fascia somewhere between the C6 and T4 vertebral levels.
- If the masticator space is involved, the infection has the potential to extend intracranially through the foramen ovale, along the course of the mandibular nerve (V3 branch of the trigeminal nerve).
- CT allows the radiologist to localize the infection accurately and distinguish a true abscess from retropharyngeal edema. Accurate diagnosis is important to avoid unnecessary and potentially harmful surgery for drainage of a reactive noninfected effusion. A true abscess appears as a rim-enhancing hypoattenuating collection that expands the retropharyngeal space and may contain foci of air.
- The degree of sinonasal mucosal thickening and opacification may be minimal and is not sensitive or specific for diagnosis of invasive fungal sinusitis in at-risk patients. Subtle stranding of the periantral fat can be the first imaging finding of vascular invasion and spread of infection beyond the sinuses.

imageOcr.markdown:
**Box 2. Elbow instability: teaching points**

1. The most important static soft tissue constraints are the LUCL and the anterior bundle of the UCL.
2. Caution should be exercised when making the diagnosis of partial UCL detachment: remember the striated appearance of the ligament.
3. UCL midsubstance disruptions account for most traumatic injuries.
4. Conventional MR imaging shows sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy that approach 100% for full-thickness UCL tears.
5. The anterior bundle of the UCL is often intact even when the radial head and coronoid process are both fractured.
6. Posttraumatic laxity, disruption, or avulsion of the LUCL is considered to be the main contributing factor in PLRI.
7. The most common injury to the LUCL is soft tissue avulsion at the proximal humeral attachment, often with concomitant injury to the common origin of the RCL.
8. Elbow dislocation is most commonly associated with a torn capsule, but the capsule may be intact if the coronoid process is fractured.
9. An abnormal posterolateral plicae usually reflects incompetence of the UCL.

【2021 官方詳解】
Thymic rebound hyperplasia
- When the body is exposed to stress, the thymus may shrink to as little as 40% of its original volume. Once the body recovers, the thymus usually grows back to its original size within 9 months; it can grow to be as much as 50% larger.
- Rebound hyperplasia is commonly seen in children but also occurs in adults
- Thymic rebound hyperplasia typically shows diffuse enlargement, a fine mixture of fat and lymphoid tissue, a smooth contour, and normal vessels; in contrast, thymic neoplasia is usually associated with a nodular contour and frequently contains necrotic or calcified foci

與cryoablation 相比，RFA 比較需要重複消融，以達到腫瘤完全壞死。
就患者舒適度而言，Cryoablation 明顯優於 RFA
一般而言，thermal ablation不適合治療大於5公分的 centrally located RCC
Cryoablation 治療中所形成的冰球範圍等同於腫瘤壞死範圍。

questions.reference: Uptodate: Radiofrequency ablation and cryoablation for renal cell carcinoma. Apr 23, 2020. updated；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p147
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Contraindications — Relative contraindications to RFA or cryoablation include:
- A life expectancy less than one year.
- The presence of distant metastases.
- Tumors >5 cm or tumors in the hilum or central collecting system are generally not candidates for ablation.
- For tumors in which treatment may cause thermal injury to the proximal ureter (resulting in urine extravasation and urinoma), an intraureteral stent is usually inserted prior to treatment.
Cryoablation
During cryoablation, the ice ball can be visualized in real time with either CT or MRI, which allows the extent of cell death to be more reliably predicted. Complete cell death is thought to occur 3 mm inside the edge of the ice ball; thus, most operators extend the ice ball at least 5 mm beyond the tumor margin to ensure complete tumor coverage.
Comparison
Local tumor progression after a single treatment session was more frequent after RFA (12.9 versus 5.2 percent with cryoablation), and repeat ablation therapy was required more often following initial treatment with RFA (8.5 versus 1.3 percent). These differences were statistically significant.

questions.questionText: Which statement about Cryoablation for renal tumor is correct?

options.text: “Rapid” cooling results in more “intracellular” ice crystal
“Slow” thawing results in microvascular occlusion and cell hypoxia
Critical temperature threshold for cell death is between −19.4°C and −40°C
An ice ball margin should be at least 5mm larger than the target tumor
All statements are correct

questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Cryoablation makes use of rapid cooling to cause cell death. Two sequential and synergistic
mechanisms lead to cell death. Intra- and extracellular ice crystals are directly cytotoxic and
lead to cell dehydration and rupture. When the frozen tissue is thawed, there is microvascular
occlusion with cell hypoxia, resulting in indirect ischemic injury.
An initial freeze followed by thawing and additional freezing (double freeze-thaw cycle) results in a larger amount of liquefaction necrosis and improves treatment efficacy.
Cell death is time- and temperature dependent, with the critical threshold for cell death being between −19.4°C and −40°C.
the goal should be an ice ball margin of at least 5 mm to avoid residual or untreated tumor.

questions.questionText: Ovarian torsion is a surgical emergency and challenging to make an accurate diagnosis, especially in pediatric population. Which of the followings is NOT correct?

options.text: Torsion of normal adnexa can occur and is more common in the pediatric population than in adults
The most commonly described finding of ovarian torsion is asymmetrical enlarged ovary
Peripherally located follicles are a specific sign of torsion in adolescents
Color Doppler US evaluation is reliable for confirming or excluding ovarian torsion
Fluid-debris level in the ovary is a specific sign of torsion in perinatal period

questions.reference: RadioGraphics 2017; 37:1892-1908.；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p152
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Color Doppler US evaluation is not reliable for confirming or excluding ovarian torsion. The absence of arterial and venous flow in the ovary and decreased venous flow are common Doppler US findings of ovarian torsion. However, these findings are nonspecific, because absent Doppler flow is frequently seen in nontorsed pediatric ovaries. Preserved arterial flow may be seen in cases of ovarian torsion—either secondary to lymphatic or venous obstruction producing symptoms before the later development of arterial occlusion, or owing to the dual arterial supply to the ovary from the uterine arteries. In adults, the twisted vascular pedicle has been described as a specific sign of ovarian torsion and can be seen as a round hyperechoic structure with multiple concentric hypoechoic stripes on transvaginal US images. However, this sign is less reliable in the pediatric population, as imaging in children is almost always performed by the transabdominal approach.

questions.questionText: At postpartum uterine imaging, it is challenging to differentiate dehiscence from normal appearance of uterine incision. Which of the followings is not CORRECT?

options.text: CT is better than pelvic MRI in imaging diagnosis
May have free fluid in peritoneal cavity
May have large bladder flap hematoma
May have pleural effusion
May show bowel distention

questions.reference: RadioGraphics 2020; 40:2117-2141.；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p154
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
At imaging, it is challenging to differentiate dehiscence from the normal appearance of the uterine incision. Accompanying signs such as free fluid, a large bladder flap hematoma (>5 cm), pleural effusion, and bowel distention have been suggested to support the diagnosis of uterine dehiscence. In the proper clinical setting, the presence of a large bladder flap hematoma and large pelvic hematomas should be considered highly suspicious for uterine dehiscence. The sensitivity of CT is poor for the diagnosis of uterine dehiscence. Pelvic MRI may provide a better diagnostic yield than does contrast-enhanced CT, because it can show the intact serosa and allow the differentiation of uterine rupture from dehiscence. The distinction is important because a ruptured uterus requires surgical repair.

questions.questionText: Which one is correct about Three-Column Classification System for tibial plateau fractures?

options.text: Zero-column tibial plateau fractures are pure articular surface depression fractures with no associated cleavage-type fracture
One-column tibial plateau fractures involve only the medial, lateral, or posterior column, with a fracture line disrupting the cortical surface of the column wall
Two-column fractures involve two of the three columns and must have two discrete fracture fragments, each of which has a fracture line extending to the cortical surface of the involved column
Three-column fractures involve all three columns of the tibial plateau, with fracture lines in each column extending to the cortical surface of the respective column wall
All above are correct

questions.reference: RadioGraphics 2021; 41:144–155；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p161
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Zero-column tibial plateau fractures are pure articular surface depression fractures with no associated cleavage-type fracture.
One-column tibial plateau fractures involve only the medial, lateral, or posterior column, with a fracture line disrupting the cortical surface of the column wall. The key to diagnosis is the presence of a split fracture with a single separate fragment in the involved column.
Two-column fractures involve two of the three columns and must have two discrete fracture fragments, each of which has a fracture line extending to the cortical surface of the involved column. For example, a lateral tibial plateau fracture would be considered a two-column fracture if there is an anterolateral fracture plus a separate posterolateral fracture fragment. This distinction is important because recent orthopedic literature advocates for an altered surgical approach to allow dorsal plating of a separate posterolateral fracture fragment for the best surgical outcome.
Three-column fractures involve all three columns of the tibial plateau, with fracture lines in each column extending to the cortical surface of the respective column wall. Three-column fractures are typically the result of high-energy trauma, resulting in highly comminuted fractures. These fractures must have at least one separate fracture fragment in each column

【2021 官方詳解】
- 結節大小 ≤4 mm ：每年一次低劑量電腦斷層。

  - 若評估為高風險，則安排開刀或切片。

questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Screening thoracic CT is appropriate for asymptomatic individuals at high risk for lung cancer . An individual’s risk for lung cancer is primarily determined by:
- Smoking history and age.
Additional risk factors include the following:
- Emphysema and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
- Interstitial lung disease, such as pulmonary fibrosis
- Occupational and environmental exposures, such as asbestos, arsenic, beryllium, cadmium, chromium, coal smoke, diesel fumes, nickel, silica, and soot
- High levels of radon(氡) exposure
- History of cancer, including lung cancer, lymphoma, head and neck cancer, and smoking-related cancers
- Family history of lung cancer
- Extensive secondhand smoke exposure
- Prior thoracic radiation therapy, as may occur for breast cancer and lymphoma

questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
- By definition, a progressive fibrosing ILD characterised by decline in lung function and early mortality. Most clinical trials and observational studies in patients with ILDs have defined disease progression in terms of decline in FVC, measured as the change from baseline in mL or as a percentage of the predicted value, or as a categorical change (typically ⩾10% predicted), or as a composite of categorical change and mortality.
- Patients with certain other types of chronic fibrosing ILD are also at risk of developing a progressive phenotype. These include idiopathic nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP), unclassifiable idiopathic interstitial pneumonia, autoimmune ILDs, chronic sarcoidosis, chronic hypersensitivity pneumonitis (HP) and exposure-related diseases such as asbestosis and silicosis
- Treatment of autoimmune ILDs usually involves corticosteroids or other immunosuppressants such as azathioprine, CYC or MMF, based on clinical experience rather than scientific evidence.

Perivesical Space.—The perivesical space is a small potential space that is enveloped by the umbilicovesical fascia. The umbilicovesical fascia fuses posteriorly with the rectovaginal fascia. The perivesical space contains the urachus (median umbilical ligament), obliterated umbilical arteries (medial umbilical folds), and urinary bladder. As with the prevesical space, the perivesical space is most commonly involved by direct tumor extension from the bladder or urachus.

Tumor extension to the iliac vessels (common and external iliac) should be scrutinized for abutment (tumor surrounding <50% of the vessel circumference), encasement (tumor surrounding >50% of the vessel circumference), and/or luminal invasion (tumor seen within the vessel) (Fig 24). At MRI, a well-defined and uninterrupted fat plane around vessels excludes involvement. Encasement of the common iliac and external iliac vessels may be a relative surgical contraindication, depending on available surgical expertise and tumor type. Vascular reconstruction with grafts may be appropriate in treatment of some tumors, such as primary soft-tissue sarcomas (23). Involvement of the internal iliac vessels is not an obstacle because, if involved, these vessels can be sacrificed owing to existing collaterals

【2021 官方詳解】
Adenomas are divided into three subtypes: tubular adenomas, tubulovillous adenomas, and villous adenomas.
Villous adenomas are one type of advanced adenoma. These lesions are typically larger than tubular adenomas—75% of them are larger than 2 cm—and they have a higher potential for malignant transformation.

In one study, investigators assessed 23 rectal villous lesions on MR images and found that the majority of them (n = 21) had a “vegetating” shape, with only two lesions characterized as flat. Most of the lesions had polycyclic margins and a thick T2-hyperintense layer along their surface, which was possibly due to high cellularity or a mucinous film coating. questions.questionText: Which of the following is a described characteristic of sporadic duodenal villous lesions?

options.text: They occur most commonly in the fourth portion of the duodenum

They have imaging features that differ from those of colonic lesions

questions.reference: Radiographics Sep-Oct 2018;38(5):1370-1384；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p214
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
In the duodenum, villous lesions can have an appearance similar to that of colonic villous lesions, but small lesions are easily missed. Sporadic duodenal villous lesions are most common in the second portion of the duodenum, and those associated with FAP are more commonly ampullary or periampullary. Small lesions may appear as nonspecific intramural nodular filling defects. Larger lesions may have a soap-bubble or cauliflower-like appearance. This appearance is that of multiple rounded radiolucent areas interspersed in a fine lacework of radiopaque material owing to barium entering the clefts between frondlike projections, as seen in the colon. Similarly, a frond- or lacelike mass in the duodenal lumen, with a feathery margin seen as contrast material enters the interstices from different directions, has been described.

questions.reference: Soft Tissue Masses of the Hand and Wrist: Systematic Approach to Imaging Evaluation, Contemporary Diagnostic Radiology: February 15, 2020 - Volume 43 - Issue 4 - p 8 ; CME Quiz. No.8; doi: 10.1097/01.CDR.0000653556.54479.2a；10.1097/01.CDR.0000653556.54479.2a；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p222
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Primary synovial osteochondromatosis is a benign synovial neoplastic process with slow formation of hyaline cartilage nodules, which calcify eventually. Tenosynovial osteochondromatosis is less frequent but can occur in the hands and feet. Calcified nodules may be visible on radiography or as dark signal on MRI. Cartilage content produces MR T2 hyperintensity. A vascularized, fibrous pseudocapsule can produce rim enhancement. If the lesion’s synovial origin is not relayed to the pathologist, the considerable cellular atypia can be misinterpreted by the pathologist as extraskeletal chondrosarcoma.

options.text: When small, T2 signal equal to fluid on MRI
Mass may have calcification on radiography
When large, “bowl of grapes” appearance on MRI
Circumscribed, nonspecific mass on ultrasound
Presentation as a painless nodule

questions.reference: Soft Tissue Masses of the Hand and Wrist: Systematic Approach to Imaging Evaluation, Contemporary Diagnostic Radiology: February 15, 2020 - Volume 43 - Issue 4 - p 8 ; CME Quiz. No.7; doi: 10.1097/01.CDR.0000653556.54479.2a；10.1097/01.CDR.0000653556.54479.2a；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p223
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Synovial sarcoma generally presents at 15 to 40 years of age as a painless nodule. Although tumor growth may be slow, these lesions have high metastatic potential; 30% have calcifications, which may be visible on radiography. A circumscribed, nonspecifi c mass is typical on ultrasound. When the lesion is small, MRI shows a homogeneous, T1 intermediate and T2 hyperintense mass. T2 signal is not quite fluid bright, and special care should be taken not to mischaracterize a small synovial sarcoma as a benign ganglionic cyst. When lesions are larger, MRI signal is heterogeneous with septations, hemorrhage, and fluid (“bowl of grapes” appearance).

questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Epidermal inclusion cysts (EICs) are the third most common soft tissue mass of the hand and often result when penetrating trauma deposits keratin-producing epithelial cells into the subdermal tissues. Consequently, they are found most commonly on the tactile surfaces of the digits. T1 and T2 signal on MRI can be variable, depending on their proteinaceous content. Calcifications are uncommon and are more suggestive of pilomatricoma (ie, a benign solitary hair follicle mass).

急性缺血中風病人若符合以下條件，應積極評估EVT治療的可能性: 年齡 ≥ 18歲；中風前的 mRS ≤ 1；NIHSS ≥ 6；開始進行介入性治療時間離中風症狀發生時間在6小時以內；和病人中 風症狀相符的ICA或MCA M1阻塞，以及腦部斷層影像ASPECTS分數 ≥ 6。
急性缺血中風病人若符合選項(B)之臨床條件，但是與中風臨床症狀相符的血管阻塞位置在 MCA M2/M3血管，仍可評估EVT的可能性。
若病患其符合EVT的治療標準，且並沒有腎功能損傷的病史，則在獲得血清肌酸酐(creatinine) 檢查結果之前，可考慮直接進行CTA檢查。

questions.questionText: 以下關於缺血性腦中風急性期的血壓控制建議，何者為非?

options.text: 未接受再灌流治療者，除了須緊急降壓的情況之外(例如嚴重的心衰竭、主動脈剝 離、高血壓腦症等)，在發生缺血性腦中風24小時內，建議收縮壓超過160 mmHg或 舒張壓超過60 mmH時開始使用降壓藥物。
符合接受靜脈血栓溶解治療者，在注射血栓溶解劑時，建議血壓控制在185/110 mmHg以下。
符合接受動脈內血栓移除治療者，若未接受靜脈血栓溶解治療，術前把血壓控制在 185/110 mmHg以下是合理的。
接受動脈內血栓移除治療者，術後24小時內將血壓維持在<180/105 mmHg是合理 的。若術後有達到成功再灌流(mTICI2b-3)，於術後24小時內將血壓維持在較低的範 圍(如<140/90 mmHg)是可以考慮的。

questions.questionText: For external acoustic canal (EAC) atresia, which one is less likely?

options.text: Dysmorphic malleus and incus

Inner ear and internal acoustic canal are usually stenotic

questions.reference: Diagnostic Imaging: Head and neck, I-2-6；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p246
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Of the syndromes resulting in microtia and EAC atresia, Goldenhar syndrome or hemifacial microsomia is the most common and is also the second most common craniofacial anomaly after cleft lip and palate. There are four major components to Goldenhar syndrome: deformity of the auricle, EAC atresia, malformation of the tympanic cavity, and ossicular abnormalities causing conductive hearing loss. Occasionally, there is also sensorineural hearing loss due to stria vascularis and semicircular canal or cochlear abnormalities as well as hypoplastic or atretic oval window. Pfeiffer syndrome is another cause of EAC stenosis/atresia that results in moderate to severe conductive or mixed hearing loss in patients with cranio-facial abnormalities. In addition to the stenosis and/or atresia of the EAC, there is hypoplasia of the middle ear cavity and occasionally hypoplastic ossicles. Typically, the inner ear anatomy is normal, but middle ear effusions are frequently seen. Therefore, when Pfeiffer syndrome patients receive CT for craniofacial anomalies, examination of the temporal bones should also be performed.

options.text: Smooth, expansile mass of middle ear

The most common cystic lesion of the petrous apex

questions.reference: Diagnostic Imaging: Head and neck, I-2 70；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p248
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Ref: Radiopaedia
Cholesterol granuloma (CG), also sometimes called a chocolate cyst of the ear or blue domed cyst, is a special type of middle ear granulation tissue which is particularly prone to bleeding and is a frequent cause of a hemotympanum. Cholesterol granulomas represent the most common cystic lesion of the petrous apex.
Radiographic features
CT
Typically, there is an expansile well-marginated lesion with thinned overlying bone. This may be dehiscent when the lesion is large. Faint peripheral enhancement post contrast may be seen.
Appearance is related to location. When a cholesterol granuloma is located in the petrous apex, it may be more aggressive in appearance, e.g. bony erosions and extension to the carotid canal or cerebellopontine angle. However, when they are located in the middle ear, associated erosion is rare.
MRI
T1: overall high signal due to cholesterol component and methemoglobin +/- low signal rim due to hemosiderin rim, and thinned adjacent bone
T2:
- central high signal +/- peripheral low signal due to hemosiderin rim
- thinned adjacent bone
- does not attenuate on FLAIR
- fat suppression: remain high signal
T1 C + (Gd): no central enhancement although faint peripheral enhancement may be difficult to see due to intrinsic high T1 signal of lesion which is not saturated (not an adipose tissue)
DWI/ADC: no restricted diffusion

questions.reference: Intracranial Vessel Wall MRI: Principles and Expert Consensus Recommendations of the American Society of Neuroradiology. AJNR Am J Neuroradiol; 2017;38:218–29；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p250
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
(A)(C)(D)如下圖 (B) Slow flow and Vasa Vasorum of major extracranial arteries may mimic vessel wall thickening, wall enhancement, and vasculitis. Most VW-MR imaging techniques rely on blood flow to achieve blood-signal suppression. Blood flow is often laminar, with lower velocity closer to the vessel wall. Incomplete signal suppression in the periphery of the lumen can mimic vessel wall thickening and/or wall enhancement. Factors predisposing to these artifacts include recirculating or slow flow within an aneurysm, low velocity flow in a dilated artery, and retrograde filling of a branch artery via leptomeningeal collaterals when there is proximal arterial occlusion.
The walls of major extracranial arteries receive blood supply through the vasa vasorum, a network of small vessels within the outer aspect of the vessel wall itself. Intracranial vessels in children lack a vasa vasorum. However, with increasing age and with atherosclerotic risk factors, extracranial vasa vasorum can extend into the proximal intracranial segments of the internal carotid and vertebral arteries. In patients with a variety of intracranial arterial diseases, a vasa vasorum can also develop distant from the extracranial vasa vasorum, with supply from nearby intracranial arteries. Vasa vasorum can cause concentric arterial wall thickening and enhancement, which mimic vasculitis.

questions.reference: Prostate Imaging Reporting & Data System - PI-RADS 2015 version 2；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p294
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Regional lymph nodes are defined as those of the true pelvis
(i.e. pelvic nodes below the bifurcation of the common iliac arteries).
common iliac arteries would be considered M1a, not N1
Clinical primary tumor staging (cT)
- TX: primary tumor cannot be assessed
- T0: no evidence of primary tumor
- T1: clinically inapparent tumor that is not palpable (image invisible)
  - T1a: tumor incidental histologic finding in 5% or less of tissue resected
  - T1b: tumor incidental histologic finding in more than 5% of tissue resected
  - T1c: tumor identified by needle biopsy found in one or both sides, but not palpable
- T2: tumor is palpable and confined within prostate
  - T2a: tumor involves one-half of one side or less
  - T2b: tumor involves more than one-half of one side but not both sides
  - T2c: tumor involves both sides
- T3: extraprostatic tumor that is not fixed or does not invade adjacent structures
  - T3a: extraprostatic extension (unilateral or bilateral)
  - T3b: tumor invades seminal vesicle(s)
- T4: tumor is fixed or invades adjacent structures other than seminal vesicles such as external sphincter, rectum, bladder, levator muscles, and/or pelvic wall
Regional nodal status (N)
Regional lymph nodes are defined as those of the true pelvis (i.e. pelvic nodes below the bifurcation of the common iliac arteries).
Nodal status is based on PSMA PET/CT, MRI or CT. On MRI/CT a 1 cm short axis diameter cut off is used if size is the sole criterion for adenopathy
- NX: regional nodes were not assessed
- N0: no positive regional nodes
- N1: metastases in regional node(s)
Distant Metastasis (M)
- M0: no distant metastasis
- M1: distant metastasis
  - M1a: non-regional lymph node(s)
    - note that a node along the common iliac arteries would be considered M1a, not N1
  - M1b: bone(s)
  - M1c: other site(s) with or without bone disease
    - e.g. lungs, liver, brain

2018 HRCT category of UIP
Classification
UIP pattern (definite)
probable UIP pattern

In 2018 the guidelines were reviewed, and the main changes compared to the 2011 publication are:
- "possible UIP" no longer exists and has been replaced by "probable UIP"
  - studies have shown that most of these patients were likely to have histopathologic UIP pattern despite the radiologic absence of honeycombing
- similar to the diagnostic HRCT criteria for usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern - Fleischner society guideline (2018), this reviewed guidelines moved from three to four HRCT categories with a reasonable correspondence among the two 2018 papers
- now, the patient's management should be based on their HRCT classification in two groups:
  - HRCT pattern of probable UIP, indeterminate for UIP, and alternative diagnosis
  - HRCT pattern of UIP

options.text: If CAC = 0, power of zero, low risk of MACE
If CAC = 0, should consider coronary CTA

All correct

questions.reference: Ahmadi A. et al JCCT 2020; 14: 394；10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.108.767665；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p336
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
When the pretest probability of coronary artery disease is low (eg, asymptomatic screening setting), a CAC score of zero is associated with low risk of coronary artery disease and low risk of near-term coronary events.
In older asymptomatic patients with risk factors, CAC=0 is associated with a moderate increased risk of events.
Patient group with clinical signs and symptoms associated with an intermediate-to-high risk of coronary disease, CAC=0 is often associated with myocardial ischemia on provocative testing (16% in their patients) and with a high risk of near-term coronary events (nearly 9 times higher than previously reported for any asymptomatic cohort). It is appropriate to question the added value of the CAC score in this moderately high-risk patient group
Ref: How Low-Risk Is a Coronary Calcium Score of Zero? The Importance of Conditional Probability
https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.108.767665 Circulation. 2008;117:1627–1629

A.
Red bone marrow has a variety of normal appearances. include smooth contiguous involvement
of bones, focal mass-like lesions, and a fine-speckled appearance.
B.
red bone marrow reconverts from yellow marrow, it does not always progress in a predictable pattern
red marrow converts to mature yellow or fatty marrow, from peripheral to central.

hands and feet tend to contain mature fatty marrow early in the maturation process, with red
marrow usually not persisting in these regions.

Red bone marrow consists of hematopoietic cells containing water and fat cells

differentiation is more problematic because of the inconsistent location and a sometimes masslike pattern of red marrow reconversion

Ultrasound usually demonstrates a non-compressible thrombosed superficial vein
MRI shows the cords were visible as low signal subcutaneous linear bands or dots

questions.reference: Breast J. 2021 Jan;27(1):44-47.；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p347
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
(以上皆對) Ref: Review of axillary web syndrome: What the radiologist should know, European Journal of Radiology
Axillary web syndrome
common after axillary surgery, frequently affecting breast cancer patients.
one or more linear bands of firm tissue, also known as “cords”, in the axilla and arm, associated with pain and limited range of motion of the shoulder and arm
Etiology:
lymphovenous tissue damage with disruption of superficial lymphatics and veins during surgery, resulting in superficial venous and lymphatic stasis and local hypercoagulability and thrombosis.
US: deformation of the dermis with shoulder abduction, an anechoic cord with hyperechoic edge, likely the lumen of a vessel and vesselwall, and hyperechoic structures thought to represent fibrosis.
no flow on Doppler images.
MRI: the cords were visible as low signal subcutaneous linear bands or dots

options.text: The goal of imaging is to localize the underlying cause, determine the extent of anatomic abnormality, and plan appropriate treatment
Ultrasound may show intraductal or intracystic, oval or lobulated mass. Lesions in the central breast are more common and often visible, while peripheral small papillomas are frequently missed

questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
Breast ductography (a.k.a. galactography)
Precisely locating the mass within breast tissue and gives useful information for surgical approach and planning.
Ref:
Diagnostic Performance of MRI Versus Galactography in Women With Pathologic Nipple Discharge: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Conclusion:
higher diagnostic performance of MRI compared with galactography in the detection of any kind of lesion with pathologic nipple discharge.
High sensitivity and very high specificity for cancer by MRI could be confirmed in this clinical setting.
If mammography and ultrasound are negative, MRI should be preferred over galactography for further evaluation.

questions.questionText: Which of the statements about the PRETEXT (PRE-Treatment EXTent of tumor) system is wrong?

options.text: The PRETEXT groups are a powerful predictor of overall survival in children with hepatoblastoma and hepatocellular carcinoma
The PRETEXT group (I, II, III or IV) is based on determining the number of contiguous tumor-free liver sections
Tumor in caudate lobe only is classified as PRETEXT I
The lungs are the most common site of distant metastases in children with hepatoblastoma and hepatocellular carcinoma

questions.reference: Pediatric Radiology (2018) 48:536–554；2021 交換考官方詳解 PDF p391
questions.explanation:
【2021 官方詳解】
C.
If tumor only involves the caudate lobe, it should be considered a PRETEXT II tumor by convention
Pediatric liver tumor staging (PRETEXT grouping system)
Used for any tumor lesion of the liver in children
The liver segments are grouped into sections:
left lateral section: segments 2 and 3
left medial section: segments 4a and 4b
right anterior section: segments 5 and 8
right posterior section: segments 6 and 7
(Only caudate lobe involvement => PRETEXT II)
PRETEXT I : one section is involved and three adjoining sections are free
PRETEXT II : one or two sections are involved, but two adjoining sections are free
PRETEXT III : tumor involves three liver sections and one liver section is free of tumor or tumor involves
two liver sections and two non-adjoining liver sections are free of tumor
PRETEXT IV: all four sections are involved, there is no liver section free of tumor
PRETEXT system divides patients into two risk groups:
high-risk group :
PRETEXT number IV
serum alpha fetoprotein <100 μg/L or very high AFP (>1 million ng/ml)
presence of additional PRETEXT criteria from groups E, H, M, N, P, and V
the rest of patients belong to the standard risk group
additional categories
caudate lobe involvement ( C)
extrahepatic abdominal disease (E)
tumor focality (F)
tumor rupture or intraperitoneal hemorrhage (H)
distant metastases (M)
lymph node metastases (N)
portal vein involvement (P)
involvement of the IVC and/or hepatic veins (V)
